sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个充满设计之爱及其相关文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至在我还在黑胶时代的夜店里当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上你都要带着300件你最珍贵的藏品去上班，然后把DJ台变成一个美丽的、有50年历史的文物的微型流动流行博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: Hey, it's Natalie, and welcome to another subscriber-only episode of The Daily.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是娜塔莉，欢迎收听《每日新闻》的订阅者专属单集。

sentences.en: We're going to be doing these bonus episodes every two weeks to bring you stories that we wouldn't normally cover on the show.
sentences.zh: 我们每两周会制作一次这些额外单集，为大家带来我们在节目中通常不会报道的故事。

sentences.en: Stories that we think are fun or interesting or just something that you, our subscribers, would enjoy.
sentences.zh: 那些我们认为有趣、好玩，或者是你们这些订阅者会喜欢的故事。

sentences.en: Here at The Daily, we have something really special and a little unusual, which is our own in-house composers.
sentences.zh: 在《每日新闻》这里，我们有一件非常特别且有点不同寻常的事情，那就是我们自己的内部作曲团队。

sentences.en: So today, a conversation with two of the people who make the music you hear on The Daily, Dan Powell and Marion Lozano.
sentences.zh: 所以今天，我们将与两位负责创作你在《每日新闻》中听到的音乐的人进行对话，他们是丹·鲍威尔和马里昂·洛萨诺。

sentences.en: For this episode, I'm turning the host mic over to someone else who's normally behind the scenes of the show, Daily producer Michael Simon Johnson.
sentences.zh: 对于这一集，我将把主持话筒交给另一位通常在节目幕后工作的人，《每日新闻》制作人迈克尔·西蒙·约翰逊。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for subscribing and, as always, for listening.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家的订阅，也一如既往地感谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: It's Saturday, October 25th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月25日，星期六。

sentences.en: Dan, Marion, thanks for sitting down to talk with me for a few minutes about music.
sentences.zh: 丹、马里昂，谢谢你们抽出几分钟时间坐下来和我聊聊音乐。

sentences.en: Thanks for having us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我们。

sentences.en: Yeah, happy to be here.
sentences.zh: 是的，很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: Listeners may not be familiar with any of us, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实，听众们可能对我们都不太熟悉。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Simon Johnson.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·西蒙·约翰逊。

sentences.en: I'm a senior producer on the show.
sentences.zh: 我是这档节目的高级制作人。

sentences.en: And what part of being a producer means is that when we work on episodes, we pick out the music to score certain sections from this growing library of tracks.
sentences.zh: 作为一名制作人，这意味着当我们制作单集节目时，我们会从这个不断扩大的音轨库中挑选音乐来为某些段落配乐。

sentences.en: And most of that music is written by a team of composers that we have, which includes the two of you.
sentences.zh: 其中大部分音乐都是由我们的作曲团队创作的，其中包括你们两位。

sentences.en: Dan, you are our creative technical manager, and you're also the composer that's been here the longeSt.
sentences.zh: 丹，你是我们的创意技术经理，也是这里资历最老的作曲家。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Marion, you've also been here quite a while.
sentences.zh: 马里昂，你在这里也待了相当长一段时间了。

sentences.en: And both of you are composers whose music we use a lot on The Daily.
sentences.zh: 你们两个都是作曲家，你们的音乐在《每日新闻》中被大量使用。

sentences.en: Honored.
sentences.zh: 深感荣幸。

sentences.en: We're super lucky to have you guys.
sentences.zh: 有你们加入我们真是太幸运了。

sentences.en: I feel grateful for you every day, and so I know a lot of the other producers do, too.
sentences.zh: 我每天都对你们心存感激，我知道其他许多制作人也是如此。

sentences.en: But you are spending a good portion of your day—I don't actually know how much—but you're spending a good portion of your week, I guess,
sentences.zh: 但你们花了一天中相当大的一部分时间——其实我不知道具体是多少——但我猜你们每周有很大一部分时间，

sentences.en: composing music that is added to this library that we pull from.
sentences.zh: 都在创作音乐，然后加入到这个供我们提取的音轨库中。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It can vary week by week, depending on the show.
sentences.zh: 这会根据每周的节目而有所不同。

sentences.en: But The Daily is by far the largest library of any of our shows, and it's probably the one we've spent the net total greatest amount of time writing music for.
sentences.zh: 但《每日新闻》到目前为止是我们所有节目中音轨库最大的一个，它也可能是我们花费总时间最多的一个音乐创作项目。

sentences.en: You're welcome.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: Yes, thank you.
sentences.zh: 是的，谢谢你们。

sentences.en: Well, I wanted to ask you guys about composing music for The Daily specifically.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想专门问问你们关于为《每日新闻》创作音乐的事情。

sentences.en: When the editorial team, when the producers and the editors are sitting around thinking about what kinds of episodes we want to make, you know, we have a certain criteria.
sentences.zh: 当编辑团队，也就是制作人和编辑们坐在一起思考我们想制作什么样的单集时，你知道的，我们有一定的标准。

sentences.en: Does this sound like a Daily episode to us?
sentences.zh: 这听起来像一期《每日新闻》吗？

sentences.en: Does this story feel like a Daily episode?
sentences.zh: 这个故事感觉像是一期《每日新闻》吗？

sentences.en: We have an idea about what that means.
sentences.zh: 我们对这意味着什么有一个概念。

sentences.en: Certain kinds of story arcs.
sentences.zh: 某些类型的故事弧线。

sentences.en: Does it have clear takeaways?
sentences.zh: 它有清晰的要点吗？

sentences.en: That kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: But I imagine for you, thinking about what The Daily means is very different.
sentences.zh: 但我猜对你们来说，思考《每日新闻》意味着什么是非常不同的。

sentences.en: So, what does making a song for The Daily mean to you?
sentences.zh: 那么，为《每日新闻》创作一首歌曲对你们来说意味着什么？

sentences.en: Well, I think the DNA of all Daily music comes from one place, which is the theme song, written by Wonderly, which is a great theme song.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为所有《每日新闻》音乐的DNA都来自一个地方，那就是由Wonderly创作的主题曲，这是一首很棒的主题曲。

sentences.en: I think it's kind of the primordial soup from which all of our cues have spawned.
sentences.zh: 我认为它有点像所有这些音轨衍生出来的原始汤。

sentences.en: And there are a few elements to that.
sentences.zh: 其中包含几个要素。

sentences.en: There's a certain amount of momentum and propulsiveness.
sentences.zh: 有一定的动感和推进力。

sentences.en: There's the instrumentation that's very heavy on strings, electric bass, electric piano.
sentences.zh: 其中的配器大量使用弦乐、电贝斯、电钢琴。

sentences.en: It feels like breaking news.
sentences.zh: 它感觉像是突发新闻。

sentences.en: It feels like current events.
sentences.zh: 它感觉像是时事。

sentences.en: It feels like the now that is happening.
sentences.zh: 它感觉像是正在发生的当下。

sentences.en: Marion, to the point of what makes something sound Daily-esque, I thought we could play a song that you wrote that is one of the most used tracks in The Daily.
sentences.zh: 马里昂，说到是什么让某些东西听起来有“每日新闻”的风格，我想我们可以播放一首你写的歌，它是《每日新闻》中最常被使用的音轨之一。

sentences.en: This one is called Looking for Answers.
sentences.zh: 这首叫做《寻找答案》。

sentences.en: I remember this one very well because I wrote it originally for an episode that never aired.
sentences.zh: 我对这首印象非常深刻，因为我最初是为一个从未播出的单集写的。

sentences.en: So, the music was released to the library, and I didn't think it would be used right away.
sentences.zh: 所以，这首音乐被发布到了音轨库中，我以为它不会马上被使用。

sentences.en: And this one was used right away.
sentences.zh: 结果这首很快就被采用了。

sentences.en: This is classic in my mind.
sentences.zh: 在我的脑海里，这堪称经典。

sentences.en: Those plucky strings, very classic Daily sound.
sentences.zh: 那些拨弦乐器，非常经典的《每日新闻》之声。

sentences.en: I think I'm using, I think it is a marimba.
sentences.zh: 我想我用的是，我觉得那是一把马林巴琴。

sentences.en: But marimba is something you guys ask me not to use.
sentences.zh: 但马林巴琴是你们要求我不要使用的乐器。

sentences.en: And sometimes I like to throw it in there as like a, see, you love it.
sentences.zh: 有时我喜欢把它加进去，就好像在说，看，你们其实很喜欢它。

sentences.en: Marimba has a kind of, it's seen internally as kind of like a cliche podcast music instrument.
sentences.zh: 马林巴琴有一种，在内部被视为一种陈词滥调的播客音乐乐器的感觉。

sentences.en: That's why.
sentences.zh: 这就是原因。

sentences.en: But the reason it's cliche is because we love it.
sentences.zh: 但它之所以成陈词滥调，是因为我们太喜欢它了。

sentences.en: So, you don't have to convince us of that.
sentences.zh: 所以，你们不必为此游说我们。

sentences.en: This song, I think, works well for The Daily because of the instrumentation within it.
sentences.zh: 这首歌之所以很适合《每日新闻》，我认为是因为其中的配器。

sentences.en: Also, it's super minimal.
sentences.zh: 另外，它极度简约。

sentences.en: So, it just works in a neutral sense because of how minimal it is.
sentences.zh: 因此，由于它的极简风格，它在一种中性的意义上发挥作用。

sentences.en: But instrumentation-wise, strings, marimba, piano.
sentences.zh: 但在配器方面，弦乐、马林巴琴、钢琴。

sentences.en: The news instruments.
sentences.zh: 新闻乐器。

sentences.en: Daily.
sentences.zh: 《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Dan, we want to play another highly used song of yours that is called The Unmaking.
sentences.zh: 丹，我们想播放另一首你创作的、被广泛使用的歌曲，叫做《解构》。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: So, The Unmaking is a type of cue that we would label as an ender.
sentences.zh: 所以，《解构》是我们会贴上“片尾曲”标签的一种音轨。

sentences.en: Meaning that this is intended to be the last piece of music you hear before the here's what else you need to know today headlines part comes in.
sentences.zh: 这意味着这是在“接下来是你今天需要知道的其他头条新闻”部分切入之前，你听到的最后一段音乐。

sentences.en: It's intentionally sparse and spread out.
sentences.zh: 它刻意保持了稀疏和舒缓。

sentences.en: Well, it also has a reflective character to it where you're sort of meant to just digest what's happened, what you've just heard,
sentences.zh: 嗯，它还具有一种反思的特质，在这里你基本上只需要消化刚刚发生的事情、你刚刚听到的内容，

sentences.en: and maybe provoke some thoughts or ruminations about the episode.
sentences.zh: 并且可能会引发对该单集的一些思考或沉思。

sentences.en: It also starts in this very, very sparse way and gradually brings in a few more things.
sentences.zh: 它也是以这种非常、非常稀疏的方式开始，然后逐渐引入更多一些元素。

sentences.en: So, there's some pizzicato strings.
sentences.zh: 所以其中有一些拨弦乐器。

sentences.en: That's that plucky string sound.
sentences.zh: 也就是那种拨弦的声音。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's live electric bass.
sentences.zh: 还有现场电贝斯。

sentences.en: Again, very, very sparse.
sentences.zh: 同样，非常、非常稀疏。

sentences.en: There's this very light drone in the background.
sentences.zh: 背景中有一种非常微弱的持续低音。

sentences.en: This is really just designed to be able to slot in in the last minute and a half of an episode in those final exchanges between the host and the reporter.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是为了能够在单集的最后分半钟内插进去，用在主持人和记者之间的最后交流中。

sentences.en: This is another popular track that we use a lot from Dan.
sentences.zh: 这是另一首我们经常使用丹的流行音轨。

sentences.en: This is Middle Distance.
sentences.zh: 这首是《中距离》。

sentences.en: So, the main instrument you're hearing in Middle Distance is a tongue drum.
sentences.zh: 所以你在《中距离》中听到的主要乐器是舌鼓。

sentences.en: It's called a tongue drum because the individual notes are cut out of the metal in the shape of a tongue, basically.
sentences.zh: 它被称为舌鼓，是因为单独的音符基本上是从金属中切出舌头形状的切口。

sentences.en: And it provides this really nice, warm, tonal sound.
sentences.zh: 它提供了这种非常美妙、温暖的音调。

sentences.en: It's particularly well-suited for podcast music because it has a rich sound, but there's not a lot going on frequency-wise in a way that would clash with vocals here.
sentences.zh: 它特别适合作为播客音乐，因为它声音丰富，但在频率上没有太多杂音，不会与这里的歌声发生冲突。

sentences.en: It's very soft and kind of muted.
sentences.zh: 它非常柔和，而且有点闷音效果。

sentences.en: There's also an electric bass and some very gentle synth and woodwind drones that enter in.
sentences.zh: 其中还加入了电贝斯以及一些非常柔和的合成器和木管乐器持续低音。

sentences.en: But this is another one of those reflective, meditative, hmm, let's ponder for a moment type of tracks.
sentences.zh: 但这也是那种反思性、沉思性、“嗯，让我们思考一会儿”类型的音轨之一。

sentences.en: All of these are, you know, I hear the first five seconds and I'm like, oh yeah, no, I know this one.
sentences.zh: 所有这些，你知道的，我一听到前五秒就会觉得，哦对，没错，我认得这个。

sentences.en: This feels like a kind of like a friend that I see around all the time.
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像一个我经常到处碰到的老朋友。

sentences.en: And it's just interesting thinking about when producers are choosing these tracks, or at least when I am listening to these tracks,
sentences.zh: 当制作人们在选择这些音轨时，或者至少当我在听这些音轨时，去思考这一点非常有趣，

sentences.en: to try to figure out which one makes the most sense.
sentences.zh: 试着弄清楚哪一个最合理。

sentences.en: I listen to them for, you know, 10, 15, 30 seconds maybe.
sentences.zh: 我听它们，你知道的，可能会听10秒、15秒、30秒。

sentences.en: And I am hearing as it's playing what I think that song is supposed to be underneath.
sentences.zh: 当它播放时，我听到的是我认为这首歌在下方应该呈现的效果。

sentences.en: But it's just funny because you have a certain idea and I have a certain idea and we haven't talked to each other about what those ideas are.
sentences.zh: 但这就很有趣，因为你有一个特定的想法，我也有一个特定的想法，而我们并没有讨论过这些想法是什么。

sentences.en: We just, there's a certain amount of truSt.
sentences.zh: 我们只是，存在着某种程度的信任。

sentences.en: You're just trusting that we have a similar idea in our heads as the producers of the show that we use these songs in the way that you were imagining.
sentences.zh: 你只是相信，作为使用这些歌曲的节目的制作人，我们脑海中有一个与你想象中相似的想法。

sentences.en: Yes, agreed.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全同意。

sentences.en: But also, it's cool when you don't have the same idea.
sentences.zh: 但同时，当你俩的想法不谋而合时也很酷。

sentences.en: It's just you envisioned it different than how we envisioned it and that's fine.
sentences.zh: 只是你设想的情景与我们设想的不同，那也没关系。

sentences.en: Because we're never telling you how we envisioned it either.
sentences.zh: 因为我们从来没有告诉你我们是怎么设想的。

sentences.en: Well, actually, that sort of brings up an interesting idea we could talk about, which is how often do you make stuff for the daily that is explicitly outside the daily-esque sound?
sentences.zh: 嗯，实际上，这确实带来了一个我们可以讨论的有趣话题，那就是，你为《每日新闻》制作明显偏离“每日新闻”风格的音乐的频率有多高？

sentences.en: How often are you sort of composing against type?
sentences.zh: 你们有多少次是在逆着类型创作？

sentences.en: When I first started working here, I was going through a sort of New York City club kid awakening and going out a lot and getting really into dance music and house and techno.
sentences.zh: 当我刚开始在这里工作时，我正经历某种纽约市夜店青年的觉醒，经常出去玩，并真正迷上了舞曲、浩室音乐和电子乐。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: And so sometimes I would be at the office late on a Friday afternoon or even evening and just make techno tracks and throw them in the daily library.
sentences.zh: 所以有时我会在周五下午甚至晚上的办公室待到很晚，只是制作电子乐音轨，然后把它们扔进《每日新闻》的音轨库里。

sentences.en: So there was a lot of experimentation of just, well, let me just make whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多关于“好吧，让我随便做点什么”的实验。

sentences.en: Maybe the daily will use this at some point.
sentences.zh: 也许《每日新闻》在某个时候会用到这个。

sentences.en: So this is one of those tracks I made.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我制作的其中一个音轨。

sentences.en: It's called 45 Hydra.
sentences.zh: 它叫做《45九头蛇》。

sentences.en: And it's just sort of a pounding, pulsing, propulsive, psychedelic techno.
sentences.zh: 它有点像那种重击、跳动、具有推进力的迷幻电子乐。

sentences.en: It has a lot of atonal and kind of just purely textural layers that warp in and out.
sentences.zh: 它有许多无调性的、纯粹质感的层次，在其中不断变形进出。

sentences.en: And I just sort of made this as a jam and then threw it in the daily Dropbox, not thinking that it would ever really get any use.
sentences.zh: 我只是把这当作一次即兴创作，然后把它扔进了《每日新闻》的Dropbox里，根本没想到它真的会被使用。

sentences.en: But then there was an episode about the WeWork founder, Adam Neumann, who had a lot of very risqué behavior as a CEO.
sentences.zh: 但后来有一期节目是关于WeWork创始人亚当·纽曼的，作为首席执行官，他有很多非常出格的行为。

sentences.en: And during one of the montages in which this was all recounted by the reporter, I heard this track pop in.
sentences.zh: 在记者讲述这一切的其中一段蒙太奇中，我听到这个音轨突然响了起来。

sentences.en: Do we want to listen to that?
sentences.zh: 我们想听听那个吗？

sentences.en: There was WeBank, there was WeSail, there was WeSleep, there was talk of an airline.
sentences.zh: 有WeBank，有WeSail，有WeSleep，甚至还有人谈论航空公司。

sentences.en: WeFly?
sentences.zh: WeFly？

sentences.en: WeFly, presumably.
sentences.zh: 大概是WeFly吧。

sentences.en: There was talk of WeMars, even putting office space on the red planet.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有人谈论WeMars，把办公室设在红色星球上。

sentences.en: That really is wild.
sentences.zh: 那真的太疯狂了。

sentences.en: It was wild.
sentences.zh: 确实很疯狂。

sentences.en: So Adam Neumann becomes fantastically rich.
sentences.zh: 所以亚当·纽曼变得极其富有。

sentences.en: He also indulges his eccentricities.
sentences.zh: 他也开始纵容自己的古怪行径。

sentences.en: I mean, he was known to walk around the office barefoot.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，众所周知他在办公室里赤脚走来走去。

sentences.en: But now he's installed a private plunge pool in his office, a cold plunge, an infrared sauna in his office.
sentences.zh: 但现在他在自己的办公室里安装了一个私人冷水浴池、一个冷水浸泡池、一个红外线桑拿房。

sentences.en: He has a white Maybach.
sentences.zh: 他有一辆白色的迈巴赫。

sentences.en: He's like glaring hip hop as this chauffeured white Maybach takes him all over Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 当这辆有专职司机的白色迈巴赫载着他穿梭于曼哈顿各地时，他把嘻哈音乐开得震天响。

sentences.en: He also convinced the company to buy a $60 million private plane, which he and other executives hotbox.
sentences.zh: 他还说服公司买了一架价值6000万美元的私人飞机，他和高管们在里面吸大麻。

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 不好意思。

sentences.en: That's, you know, getting high in a confined space with the marijuana smoke filling the cabin.
sentences.zh: 那是，你知道的，在密闭空间里嗨大麻，大麻烟雾充满整个机舱。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is amazing.
sentences.zh: 是的，这太棒了。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm mainly just proud I could provide the soundtrack to Michael learning what hotboxing is for the first time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我主要是为自己能为迈克尔第一次了解什么是吸大麻提供配乐而感到自豪。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Jokes aside, I have this bit I sometimes say that everything I learned about podcast music I learned from club music.
sentences.zh: 玩笑归玩笑，我有时会说这样一句话：我从播客音乐中学到的一切都是从夜店音乐中学到的。

sentences.en: And I'm only half kidding because they are actually serving really similar functional roles.
sentences.zh: 我这话可不是开玩笑，因为它们实际上在发挥着非常相似的功能。

sentences.en: Tell us more.
sentences.zh: 跟我们多讲讲。

sentences.en: So podcast music has to be repetitive and minimal in a way where you have things that are repeating so as not to distract the listener.
sentences.zh: 所以播客音乐必须具有重复性和极简性，你要有重复的元素以免分散听众的注意力。

sentences.en: Minimal so as not to take away from the voice of the people talking.
sentences.zh: 极简是为了不抢夺说话者的声音。

sentences.en: But there also needs to be just the right amount of variation because if it's too repetitive, it's just going to sound like a loop and get old and feel very,
sentences.zh: 但同时也需要恰到好处的变化，因为如果它太重复，听起来就会像个循环，变得陈旧，感觉非常、

sentences.en: very stale and stagnant.
sentences.zh: 非常陈腐和停滞不前。

sentences.en: And the listener will become aware of the music in a way that they shouldn't.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，听众就会以一种不该有的方式注意到音乐。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which we don't want.
sentences.zh: 这是我们不希望看到的。

sentences.en: Dance music can actually be very similar in that you're often trying to make things that repeat and vary a little bit over time but also not so much because things need to stay in a consistent groove.
sentences.zh: 舞曲其实也十分类似，因为你通常努力在创作一些随时间不断重复又略有变化的东西，但又不能变太多，因为必须要保持稳定连贯的律动。

sentences.en: So who knows?
sentences.zh: 所以谁知道呢？

sentences.en: Maybe the two are, you know, cross-disciplinary musical studies or maybe I'm just trying to justify my, you know, off-hours music tastes into my day job.
sentences.zh: 也许这两者是，你知道的，跨学科的音乐研究，或者我只是在试图把我的，你知道的，下班后的音乐品味合理化，当成我日常工作的一部分。

sentences.en: As having a professional value.
sentences.zh: 赋予其职业价值。

sentences.en: I think it does.
sentences.zh: 我觉得是的。

sentences.en: I can hear it in the music that you write for us and not just the electronic music but also I feel very conscious of those small variations that you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 我能从你为我们创作的音乐中听出来，不仅是电子音乐，而且我能真切感受到你所说的那些微小变化。

sentences.en: They're good.
sentences.zh: 它们很棒。

sentences.en: I feel so seen.
sentences.zh: 我感觉自己被看透了。

sentences.en: Marianne, what kind of music have you written for the show that is the kind of offbeat, non-daily sound?
sentences.zh: 玛丽安，你为节目写过什么样那种非同寻常的、非日常的音乐？

sentences.en: Bed-Stuy.
sentences.zh: 贝德斯图伊。

sentences.en: 90s hip-hop.
sentences.zh: 90年代嘻哈。

sentences.en: I named this track off of the neighborhood Bed-Stuy in Brooklyn because that's where Bay is from.
sentences.zh: 我用布鲁克林的贝德斯图伊这个社区给这首曲子命名，因为拜伊就是那里的人。

sentences.en: And it was originally written for an episode, Rest in Peace, that did not air on 50 Years of Hip-Hop.
sentences.zh: 它最初是为一集未在《嘻哈五十年》中播出的节目《安息吧》写的。

sentences.en: Yes, I was working on that episode.
sentences.zh: 是的，我当时正在制作那一集。

sentences.en: I was very excited about it.
sentences.zh: 我对此感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: It did not air.
sentences.zh: 它没有播出。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: R.I.P.
sentences.zh: R.I.P.

sentences.en: Hip-hop and R&B are my favorite genres of music.
sentences.zh: 嘻哈和R&B是我最喜欢的音乐流派。

sentences.en: So any excuse to write in that vein, I'm all over.
sentences.zh: 所以只要有借口写这种风格的歌，我都义不容辞。

sentences.en: So yeah, I wrote this song that has that classic boom-bap sound, the kick and the snare.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我写了这首歌，带有经典的Boom-bap之声，有底鼓和军鼓。

sentences.en: Very crisp percussion.
sentences.zh: 非常清脆的打击乐。

sentences.en: Yeah, and then there is a bass line and a guitar line that are playing on a loop.
sentences.zh: 对，然后有一条低音线和一条吉他线在循环播放。

sentences.en: And that's intentional because 90s hip-hop is very much a rapper laying bars over a loop.
sentences.zh: 这是刻意为之的，因为90年代的嘻哈很大程度上就是说唱歌手在循环乐段上说唱。

sentences.en: And these loops, I mean,
sentences.zh: 而这些循环乐段，我是说，

sentences.en: the guitar and the bass also sound like they are derived from some funk song that you found somewhere on an old vinyl in the same way that 90s hip-hop producers would.
sentences.zh: 吉他和贝斯听起来也像是从你不知在哪张旧黑胶唱片上找到的某首放克歌曲里提取出来的，就像90年代的嘻哈制作人那样。

sentences.en: Well, I wanted it to just sound a little gritty like it was something ripped from a vinyl.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我只是想让它听起来带点粗砺感，就像是从黑胶唱片上截取的一样。

sentences.en: So yeah, I like samples.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我喜欢采样。

sentences.en: Sort of a strange question for you guys.
sentences.zh: 对你们来说可能算是个奇怪的问题。

sentences.en: What do you hope that listeners take away from the music?
sentences.zh: 你们希望听众从音乐中获得什么？

sentences.en: Because on the one hand, you're musicians.
sentences.zh: 因为一方面，你们是音乐人。

sentences.en: I imagine that when you envisioned being a musician, it was to create music that you wanted people to listen to.
sentences.zh: 我想象当你们设想成为一名音乐人时，是为了创作人们想听的音乐。

sentences.en: But the nature of the music that you're writing is to be a little bit more invisible on some level.
sentences.zh: 但你们创作的音乐的性质，在某种程度上是为了更加隐形一些。

sentences.en: And making music, as you said earlier, Dan, that is too noticeable sort of defeats the whole point of this.
sentences.zh: 正如你刚才所说，丹，如果制作出过于显眼的音乐，就有点违背这背后的全部意义了。

sentences.en: So I'm curious about how you think about the listeners engaging with your music.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇你们是如何看待听众与你们的音乐产生互动的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I like to think of music and podcasts as highlighter, especially in moments that are very explainary.
sentences.zh: 对，我倾向于把音乐和播客中的音乐看作荧光笔，尤其是在解释性很强的时刻。

sentences.en: I think sometimes a listener can tune out for a second.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有时听众可能会走神一会儿。

sentences.en: And I think of our music as a way to highlight a section.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们的音乐可以起到突出某一部分的作用。

sentences.en: And we got to keep it interesting, but not distracting at the same time.
sentences.zh: 我们既要保持它的趣味性，同时又不能喧宾夺主。

sentences.en: So there are a lot of layers to it.
sentences.zh: 所以这里面有很多层面的考量。

sentences.en: But I think in general, when I think about the listener, I think about drawing them back in.
sentences.zh: 但总体而言，当我考虑到听众时，我想的是如何把他们的注意力重新吸引回来。

sentences.en: Well, like I said before, I feel the trust that you put in us as producers to use your music adequately and in a way that honors the intention of it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就像我之前说的，我能感受到你们作为制作人对我们的信任，能够恰如其分地使用你们的音乐，并以尊重其原意的方式来使用。

sentences.en: And if I haven't expressed this sufficiently enough, I feel very grateful that you guys do what you do, that you do it for this show.
sentences.zh: 如果我还没表达得足够充分的话，我真的很感激你们能做你们所做的事，为这个节目做这些。

sentences.en: All of the producers and editors consider the music very, very essential to the show.
sentences.zh: 所有的制作人和剪辑师都认为音乐对这个节目来说非常非常重要。

sentences.en: So, Dan, Marion, thank you so much for stopping by.
sentences.zh: 所以，丹、玛丽安，非常感谢你们来到这里。

sentences.en: Thank you for having us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: And something we're very grateful to do on our end as well.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们在自己这边非常感激能做的事。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对的。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: We just want to make your life easier when it's 4 a.m.
sentences.zh: 我们只是想在凌晨四点时让你们的生活轻松一点，

sentences.en: And you need to find, you know, something that you put in like, oh, God, how am I going to end this?
sentences.zh: 当时你需要找点什么东西放进去，然后想：天哪，我该怎么结尾？

sentences.en: That's so real.
sentences.zh: 太真实了。

sentences.en: That's like not an exaggeration.
sentences.zh: 这可真不是夸张。

sentences.en: So I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的很感激。

sentences.en: I hope it's not 4 a.m.
sentences.zh: 但愿不是凌晨四点。

sentences.en: I hope it's more like 3 a.m.
sentences.zh: 但愿更像是凌晨三点。

sentences.en: Yeah, sometimes it's midnight.
sentences.zh: 对，有时是午夜。

sentences.en: And that's always nice.
sentences.zh: 那总是挺好的。

sentences.en: Thanks, guys.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Michael Simon Johnson and Rochelle Bonja.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由迈克尔·西蒙·约翰逊和罗谢尔·邦贾制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lexi Diao and Paige Cowett.
sentences.zh: 由莱克茜·刁和佩奇·考特剪辑。

sentences.en: Contains music by Dan Powell and Marion Lozano.
sentences.zh: 包含丹·鲍威尔和玛丽安·洛扎诺创作的音乐。

sentences.en: And was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.en: I'm Natalie Kietroev.
sentences.zh: 我是娜塔莉·基特罗耶夫。

sentences.en: See you next time.
sentences.zh: 下次见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一个受到严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了（上台）一批自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就陷入了一场激烈、混乱有时又惊心动魄的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在我和萨拉·科尼格主持的最新一期《都市》节目中，将讲述人们试图维持其影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在你获取播客的任何地方收听。

sentences.en: Here's a bit.
sentences.zh: 这是一个片段。

sentences.en: Here's the story.
sentences.zh: 这就是故事。

sentences.en: Next time.
sentences.zh: 下期再见。

sentences.en: Let's go.
sentences.zh: 我们走吧。
